title: The 8 Levels of 'We Need to Talk'
house: Fruit City, a bustling metropolis where every resident is a walking piece of produce with a glowing digital number on their forehead, navigating life based entirely on their mysterious status badge.
catchphrase: The number never lies, but it always hurts.
links: The barista in Level 2 mentions the regular customer in the tailored suit who leaves massive tips.
The bus route 42 from Level 4 is seen delayed in the background of Level 1.
The neon kiosk from Level 5 sells the exact same bruised apples that fall in Level 7.

levels.name: Mia, 22, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of the dreaded intro. Level 1. Level 1: Zero minutes of warning before my boyfriend drops the dreaded four-word bomb in a crowded diner. I'm Mia, 22, staring at my half-eaten blueberry muffin while my forehead glows a brutal zero. We need to talk. You never gave me any notice about your chaotic schedule, so I am leaving right now. Just pay for your muffin and clear the table, honey. People are waiting. The coffee cups clattered loudly against the saucers as the entire room suddenly fell into an uncomfortable silence. My hands trembled violently against the laminate table while my digital status flickered between life and total system error. He smirked, crossed his arms, and leaned in closer to drop a devastating twist that shattered my entire world. Just when I thought things could not possibly get any worse, a mysterious notification popped up on my cracked phone screen. Then he dropped that one chilling sentence that made the entire room go dead silent ... You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Sam, 26, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of the dreaded intro. Level 2. Level 2: Twelve and a half minutes of warning before my boss hands me an eviction notice disguised as a performance review. I'm Sam, 26, steaming oat milk in a cramped café while my zesty lemon skin tingles with cold sweat. We need to talk about your future here. Your lack of preparation is dragging down our entire morning rush, so clean out your locker by noon. Don't worry, Sam. That guy yells at everyone before his morning espresso. The steam wand hissed aggressively, drowning out the ambient jazz music while my colleagues avoided eye contact entirely. A strange man in a tailored dark suit lingered near the entrance, watching every single move I made with intense suspicion. Suddenly, the espresso machine sputtered and died, leaving me stranded in front of a long line of impatient customers. I tried to reset the breaker, but the digital display on the wall flashed an alarming red warning code. Then he flashed that arrogant grin and whispered ... You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Chloe, 29, Florist
levels.story: The 8 levels of the dreaded intro. Level 3. Level 3: Forty-five minutes of warning before my landlord cancels my greenhouse lease with a cold smile. I'm Chloe, 29, arranging crimson tulips in a drafty warehouse while my delicate rosepetal cheeks tremble. We need to talk about your overdue rent. Your botanical boutique isn't generating enough foot traffic, so hand over the keys right now. Ignore him, Chloe! Your roses are the only bright spot on this whole dreary street. Rain hammered against the fragile glass roof of the greenhouse as the temperature inside plummeted rapidly. My prized orchids began to wither under the sudden draft, echoing the icy atmosphere in the room. He slammed a thick leather-bound ledger onto my workbench, revealing a hidden clause that completely undermined my contract. A courier rushed past the window, throwing a package onto the muddy welcome mat before sprinting away. Then he whispered that terrifying ultimatum ... You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Maya, 24, Travel Blogger
levels.story: The 8 levels of the dreaded intro. Level 4. Level 4: Two and a half hours of warning before my editor cancels my international flight and strips my press pass. I'm Maya, 24, packing a battered vintage suitcase in a sunlit loft while my dragonfruit skin radiates bright magenta and green. We need to talk about your travel budget. Your engagement metrics dropped yesterday, so we are reallocating your ticket to someone else. Don't let them ground you, Maya! Your travel stories inspire half this city. My passport sat open on the wooden desk, surrounded by expired tickets and stamped postcards from faraway adventures. The television in the background blared breaking news about municipal budget cuts affecting independent journalists. She checked her luxury gold wristwatch and tapped her polished high heel against the hardwood floor impatiently. An urgent message flashed across my laptop screen, revealing that my entire destination had been secretly altered. Then she flashed a cold smirk and said ... You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Leo, 31, Technician
levels.story: The 8 levels of the dreaded intro. Level 5. Level 5: Twelve hours of warning before my network supervisor shuts down our municipal grid access. I'm Leo, 31, soldering microchips in a neon-lit basement while my sleek avocado skin glistens under fluorescent tubes. We need to talk about your system diagnostics. Your firewall update missed the morning deadline, so I am revoking your master key. Don't let him lock you out, Leo! We need your code to keep the whole block online. Sparks flew from the motherboard as I frantically typed the override sequence into the primary terminal. Sirens wailed softly in the distance, signaling an approaching system lockdown that threatened every resident in the city. He pulled a heavy master override card from his pocket and dangled it just out of reach with a mocking smile. Suddenly, every monitor in the subterranean facility flickered and displayed a mysterious countdown timer. Then he gave a wicked chuckle and dropped this hint ... You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Elena, 35, Architect
levels.story: The 8 levels of the dreaded intro. Level 6. Level 6: Three days of warning before my senior partner strips my name from the skyscraper master plan. I'm Elena, 35, sketching blueprints on a glass table in a glass-walled skyscraper while my crisp pear skin glows with quiet determination. We need to talk about your design budget. Your eco-tower concept is too costly for our investors, so we are handing the project to someone else. Don't let them steal your blueprints, Elena! That tower is entirely your vision. The skyline glowed in fiery orange hues as the sun dipped below the horizon, casting long shadows across the architectural models. My colleagues stood by in stunned silence, realizing that corporate greed had finally overtaken our artistic integrity. He tossed my revised portfolio onto the floor with a resounding crash that echoed through the empty office. Before I could pick up the scattered papers, my phone buzzed with an unauthorized transfer alert from the company vault. Then he offered a condescending smile and declared ... You'll see that in Level 7.
